context: Extend agent_instruction_audit.py to scan all governed docs for authority claims and fail when more than one document claims to win or a superseded doc self-describes as canonical; repoint test_blind_spot_tools.py and AGENTS.md bindings to the selected authority; update the SHARED/review-protocol canonical skill lockstep reference if it names the legacy path (canonical-side edit rides the item-1 promotion flow).
description: PR #1318 introduces docs/development/agent-review-protocol.md claiming to supersede docs/development/review-protocol.md, but the legacy doc still declares itself 'Canonical, unabridged form' and says it wins conflicts, and active consumers (.claude/commands/blind-spot.md, tests/unit/scripts/test_blind_spot_tools.py:37-42 which ASSERTS the legacy binding, _project/blind-spots/README.md, _project/specs/findings-domain.md) still bind to the legacy path. The audit script only inspects the new doc and cannot see the conflict. This item covers the audit-side surfaces; the legacy doc, command, README, validator and specs surfaces belong to existing item blind-spot-command-protocol-alignment-20260724 (scope is create-time-only, so the split is structural). Both items MUST land in the same PR (#1318) - the blind-spot item's own anti-pattern forbids flipping surfaces in separate commits; one PR for two TODOs is the documented exception to one-TODO-per-PR, justified by the no-contradiction-window invariant. Decision: demote the legacy doc to an explicitly non-authoritative historical pointer rather than delete (external references exist, e.g. user-global config and the SHARED/review-protocol canonical skill lockstep note); rejected alternative: deletion, which breaks inbound references and loses the unabridged rationale.
